title: Mahatma Gandhi
shortDescription: A leader who made nonviolent mass action a force in the independence movement.
description: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi connected political freedom with everyday acts of discipline, solidarity and self-reliance. Satyagraha—truth-force—shaped campaigns from Champaran and Kheda to the Non-Cooperation, Salt and Quit India movements.

title: Bhagat Singh
shortDescription: A revolutionary thinker whose writing and sacrifice galvanised young Indians.
description: Bhagat Singh joined revolutionary networks while still a teenager and read widely in politics, history and atheism. His courtroom statements and hunger strike turned his trial into a platform for anti-colonial ideas, and his execution in 1931 made him an enduring symbol of resistance.
keyFacts: Helped found the Naujawan Bharat Sabha
Threw non-lethal bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly

title: Subhas Chandra Bose
shortDescription: A nationalist leader who sought international support for India’s liberation.
description: Subhas Chandra Bose believed that the British Empire would not leave India through petitions alone. During the Second World War he led the Indian National Army and formed the Provisional Government of Free India, making the call “Give me blood, and I will give you freedom.”
keyFacts: President of the Indian National Congress in 1938 and 1939

title: Gandhi Salt March
shortDescription: A 390-kilometre walk that made the humble salt crystal a symbol of empire’s injustice.
description: On 12 March 1930, Gandhi and 78 companions left Sabarmati Ashram for the coastal village of Dandi. By breaking the colonial salt law on 6 April, the march invited people across India to join civil disobedience and made an everyday necessity a national political language. This interactive 3D model presents the sculpted tableau of the Salt Satyagrahis on the march.
keyFacts: Started on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram
Sparked nationwide civil disobedience and boycott of colonial monopolies
